Training coverage and the underlying machine-learning ideation task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds AI-Scientist-V2 with a Sonnet backbone to the ICLR comparison and a direct-generation Full-SFT comparator to the motivation ablation. V1's AI-Scientist-V2 (Claude) is retained as Haiku with identical scores; this is a clarified name, not a replacement.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include direct-versus-two-stage Full-SFT controls, an additional 60-sample NeurIPS human-validation study, and entropy analysis of 100 training samples using heuristic token categories. Existing metrics and training hyperparameters remain unchanged. The clarified 4,000 SFT samples and approximately 2,000 RL prompts agree with v1 Appendix B.

E4.justification: V2 adds motivation-conditioning controls, venue-shift robustness and evaluator validation, analysis testing whether entropy masking selects technical content, and three reasoning-behavior case studies. These substantially extend the original reward, entropy-threshold, and length-anchoring ablations, which remain intact.

E5.justification: Appendix I introduces 95% bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples, Bonferroni-corrected Welch tests, and Cohen's d. Appendix E adds inter-annotator reliability with a confidence interval and within-one-point agreement. Averaging three LLM evaluations per sample was already documented in v1.

E6.justification: Original ICLR scores remain unchanged, including MoRI's 3.19 mean. V2 adds NeurIPS and combined means of 3.15 and 3.18, Sonnet-backed AI-Scientist-V2's ICLR mean of 3.14, and direct/two-stage Full-SFT means of 2.75/2.85 on NeurIPS. New findings include token-selection statistics and nonsignificance against Claude-3.5-Sonnet. These are additional comparisons, not matched-setting performance improvements.

M1.justification: The base model, SFT/RL stages, EAIG and CSG rewards, length anchoring, and cascaded inference remain unchanged. The explicit entropy formula clarifies the existing calculation. The epsilon added to the inline GRPO formula was already present in v1 Figure 2.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, removes a duplicated evaluation-prompt paragraph, expands the performance discussion, and adds acknowledgments and analysis subsections. The original narrative and section sequence remain largely intact; the added scientific material does not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 2 becomes a full-width comparison with ICLR, NeurIPS, and combined-result groups. New displays cover motivation controls, topical distributions, entropy statistics, evaluator agreement, uncertainty, input/prompt examples, and reasoning behaviors. Original diagrams, training plots, and worked examples are retained with relocation and renumbering.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds a focused distinction from verifier-free, reference-probability approaches: multiple valid long-form methodologies make lexical probability rewards noisy. The broader positioning remains unchanged. Guo-to-DeepSeek-AI attribution and expanded author lists concern the same cited works.

T1.justification: Appendix F's assumptions and length-bias derivations are retained. The added predictive-entropy expression formalizes the existing mask calculation, while the inline epsilon reconciles the text with v1 Figure 2. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical argument is introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens an evaluation previously confined to one venue: it adds venue-shift testing, a stronger agentic comparator, and controls separating motivation conditioning from RL. Confidence intervals, corrected tests, and additional human validation make the evidence more assessable and reveal that superiority over Claude-3.5-Sonnet is not significant. These address important weaknesses in empirical support, although coverage remains within machine learning and feasibility is still assessed through judgments.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoRI research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds NeurIPS evaluations, further controls, token analyses, statistical comparisons, and human-validation results.

before.justification: V1 reports original scientific-ideation evaluations, human–LLM agreement measurements, reward ablations, training dynamics, and generated examples.
